_comment: The ONE table of cases for the name-token rule, read by BOTH implementations:
The rule is a normalised-token match, not an edit distance: 'Jansari Jaydatt' and
'Jaydatt Jansari' are the same human and no sensible edit distance says so, while
'Aarav' and 'Aarti' are different humans and a loose edit distance says they are not.
Every person in this file is INVENTED. The repo is public.
`tokens` is the expected set, order-insensitive. See docs/M3_PLAN.md §3 for why both
implementations had to change to agree on it.

cases.name: Jansari Jaydatt
cases.why: the base case

cases.name: Jaydatt Jansari
cases.why: word order must not matter — the case BUILD_PROMPT_M3 names

cases.name: Jaydatt   Jansari
cases.why: double spaces and padding collapse

cases.name: JAYDATT JANSARI
cases.why: case folds

cases.name: जयदत्त जांसरी
cases.why: Devanagari: the virama and the vowel signs are PART of the word, not separators. The Kotlin rule used to split here, yielding जयदत + सर

cases.name: જયદત્ત જાંસરી
cases.why: Gujarati: the TypeScript rule used to produce an EMPTY set, which findDuplicates reads as 'no duplicates' for every such person

cases.name: ஜெயதத் ஜான்சரி
cases.why: Tamil: same failure as Gujarati on the server side

cases.name: জয়দত্ত জানসারি
cases.why: Bengali

cases.name: ಜಯದತ್ತ ಜಾನಸರಿ
cases.why: Kannada

cases.name: José Álvarez
cases.why: accented Latin: the server used to give jos + lvarez, so the two sides disagreed about whether two records were one person

cases.name: Zoë
cases.why: a single accented token survives the two-character floor

cases.name: Jose Alvarez
cases.why: KNOWN LIMIT: this does NOT match José Álvarez. Stripping diacritics means stripping combining marks, which is exactly what breaks every Indic name above

cases.name: Anne-Marie Dsouza
cases.why: a hyphen separates

cases.name: O'Brien
cases.why: the apostrophe separates and the one-letter O is below the floor — deliberate, and the reason a one-token name can still match on a surname

cases.name: Dr. Meera Raghunathan
cases.why: a title is a token; it is common to both records or to neither

cases.name: R. K. Narayanan
cases.why: single-letter initials fall below the floor; the surname carries the match

cases.name: Aarav Shah 2
cases.why: a single digit is below the floor too

cases.name: Priya (work)
cases.why: brackets separate; a disambiguating note becomes its own token
no tokens. findDuplicates must return nothing rather than matching everyone
whitespace only

cases.name: A B
cases.why: every token below the floor — same as empty

duplicate_pairs.why: a title does not make a second person
they share a surname, so the NAME rule matches — the day/month check is what separates them. This is why dedup is name tokens PLUS a date, never name alone
no shared token. A loose edit distance would call these one person; this rule does not
the Gujarati case that used to match NOTHING on the server
a first name alone is a legitimate match
the known limit, stated as a case so it is a decision and not a surprise
